commit.message: Add another Crazy Yiuf line.

Don't let Breathe Rust make clouds on two sides of a wall at once

If the player was standing such that they could see both sides of a wall,
Breathe Rust could place clouds on both of it simultaneously, eg:

...@..
...#..
§§§#§.
§§§#§.
§§§#§.

Instead, use a standard explosion calculation and pick the first X tiles
out of that (which should also match the targeting UI most directly).

Fix multiple oddities with the Breathe Rust targeter (Flugkiller)

The targeter was calculating the 'explosion' of clouds as if the beam
didn't penetrate targets, but still drawing main path of the beam as if it
did, leading to some very odd and inscrutible shapes.

On top of this, tiles that 'might' be in the radius of effect (if the
player's power is insufficient to fill all of radius 2) were overriding
tiles that will definitely be affected (due to being in the beam's path
itself), contributing to 'gaps' in the affected area. I don't think there
are any other beam-based 'explosions' of variable radius in Crawl at the
moment, but this would have affected those as well.

Finally, the targeter was misleading about this ability's capability to
affect wall monsters. Since its only effect is to place clouds, it can't
affect monsters inside walls in any way, and should convey this more
properly.

Let crab form double archery ego

Crabs are our friends and want to have fun. Let your crab shoot a giant gun.

Fix crash with wall monsters and gavotte

They were crashing when being gavotted into the level boundary. Now they
stop there (with no collision)
Fix some mapstat option parsing

Fix a ziggurat entry vault (rypofalem)

When 2a440f7 updated this ziggurat to use ; instead of ', it did not
update the opaque KMASK. This made the area in the middle look
disconnected and prevented the vault from generating.

Fix an overflow vault that never placed (rypofalem)

3b09176 attempted to fix an issue where we occasionally placed this
vault without stairs, but in doing so it made it unplaceable as it falls
foul of the "do not increase dungeon regions" connectivity check. We
have now fixed the stair problem in a more robust way by banning random
stair removal from touching vaults, so we revert this transparent tag.

The other vault in the same commit is fine to stay transparent, because
it is primary and therefore allowed to disconnect the level.

Do not cull random vault stairs

We used to do four passes of stair-culling:
- Redundant (i.e. walkable-between), non-vault
- Redundant vault
- Random non-vault
- Random vault

The last of these is somewhat unsafe; vaults can rely on stairs for
connectivity, and can be opaque so that connectivity checks won't catch
when this fails. So we remove the last pass; when we would have reached
it we now veto the level. Now that the parent commit fixes stair
culling, this veto is vanishingly rare; in fact in a 500 game mapstat
run there were no instances of it that wouldn't have been vetoed later
as the random stair removal disconnected the level.

Cull redundant stairs better

The comments in the _cull_redundant_stairs function state that it
iterates through stairs if there are more than 3, removing some that are
reachable from other stairs by walking. This is very sensible, as it
means that we remove stairs without breaking connectivity.

However, this isn't what it was actually doing. Instead, it was
iterating through the stairs, removing some that share a type of stair
(e.g. "upstair 2") that is reachable from other stairs by walking. This
could cull arbitrary stairs and leave disconnected regions.

Fix listing of sound in features on ?V

SOUND_BACKEND was missing from command.cc

fix sound conditional in initfile.cc

As currently written, all four defines must exist. But three of them are
intended to be platform-specific and it's not really expected that more
than one of them be defined.

Fix marshalling and unmarshalling of stack flags

This fixes a bug introduced in 2985acf whereby the stash always loaded
zeroed flags on reload, which made autoexplore think stashes were
unvisited and revisit them.

Fixes #5369

Fix monster barding pickup logic being inverted

Monsters who were supposed to be able to pick up and wear bardings were the
only species that were explicitly forbidden from doing so. Whoops.

This fixes #5367

Fix FHEIGHT often having no effect (nicolae)

The height of a feature can be set by a vault using FHEIGHT. However,
this would often not work as the height would get accidentally
overridden when placing the Shoals layout or when giving features in
vaults default heights.

Improve setting of water and floor height in Shoals vaults

We were often setting all floors to the same height and all shallow
water squares to the same height. This would cause tides to flood the
whole vault at the same time rather than gradually move in. It would
also cause wave animations to show a wave everywhere in the vault at
once rather than showing a moving wave.

Instead, make floors farther from water higher and shallow water closer
to floors higher.

Rework making sure squares don't get bad flavour during level gen

If a vault places a feature and then level generation replaces the
feature, we need to remove the tile override and also reset the squares
colour.

Unfortunately, we had multiple ways of achieving this. The first way was
that we would call _set_grd to replace the feature. However, some places
that replaced a feature did so by directly altering env.grid and making
sure every where that needed to call _set_grd did was rather hard. The
second way was that we would not show "feat" tile overrides on floor
tiles so that if a squares that had a "feat" tile override was replaced
with a floor the incorrect tile override wouldn't be shown. The third
way was that we would keep track of which features had been placed by
vaults and reset the squares colour after generating the level if the
feature was different from what the vault had placed.

The third way can be adapted to handle resetting tile overrides,
allowing us to remove the first and second ways. However, I haven't yet
allowed floors to show "feat" tile overrides as we still have a few ways
that these can end up incorrect on floors outside of level generation.

Fix a possible A screen crash in wizmode

When you lower your level in wizmode, innate mutations that were gained
from levelling up are not removed. This can cause A's description of future
mutations to attempt to query mutation levels higher than 3 (eg: if a
vine stalker had fangs 3, then lowered their level below 8, the game would
think they would gain fangs 4 at XL 8 and then crash).

Properly cleaning up innate mutations would be nicer, but let's at least
not crash.

Redraw tentacle segments more promptly

This fixes a little flicker on webtiles where we draw the removal of the
old segments before the addition of the new ones.

Don't create a stash at the player's position every time we load any

The default constructor for Stash set its position to the player's, if none
was specified. This was, as far as I can tell, only used when loading
existing stashes from a save file. Which meant that every single stash
loaded would first intialize itself from whatever was at the player's
position before wiping all that out to load the intended data.

This is a bit pointless and wasteful, but also could create odd errors in
some cases. For instance, the lua tables handling portal markers were not
fully loaded before stashes were, which could result in a massive number of
lua errors when loading a save file where the player was on top of a portal
(as every stash on the level would attempt to read from a table for the
marker at the player's feet). This became more obvious after d744bac fully
reset lua state when the game was reset.

Now we only fully initialize a stash if given an in-bounds position and
don't remap (0,0) to the player's location. (As far as I can tell, this was
only used prior to loading, which should overwrite all state anyway.)

This fixes #5363

Make the abyss shift at the same rate in all directions

This removes an incentive to walk North/South rather than East/West in
order to trigger more shifts and find the rune faster. This incentive
was minor compared to the need to avoid danger, but this way nobody has
to think about it.

Move abyssal shift to world_reacts

We previously checked the abyss shift on player movement. This meant
that if a player moved only through less pedestrian means, such as
scrolls of blinking, they could reach the edge of the abyss. This was
bad both because reaching the edge of the infinite abyss is surprising,
and because it was rather buggy there, with the abyss shifting every
turn without recentering the player. So now we check for a shift every
turn.

Kill tentacles via their heads

When we kill a tentacle segment, we now kick the real (non-reset) death
up to the head, and have it clean up all the tentacles. This means that
we consistently process the head death properly. This mostly matters for
eldritch tentacles, where we now grant XP, immediately remove eldritch
portals, give a custom message, and count the monster as vanquished.

We also remove a block of code that looked like it was doing the same
thing, but never fired.

Fixes #5361

Add owned counts to shopping list (particleface)

This is consistent with the change for shops in a221df3
Update credits

Remove you.prev_grd_targ

After getting yet another bug report about the targeting cursor sticking to
things it shouldn't, I am feeling like dfde840 was misguided and that that
it would have been better to cut this code (which had been unknowingly
nonfunctional for a couple of versions) than reenable it.

While I'd thought it would be mildly helpful in a few situations, it's
turning out to have much larger negative effects in more situations than it
would have had positive ones.

(Really, it might be nice to have that sort of memory operate on the basis
of each individual thing being aimed, but it seems tricky to do this (there
is no unified way to refer to spells/abilities/items and there are multiple
things beyond that which use this interface.))

Don't retain cursor memory after casting hellfire mortar (adinsx)

The spot the player aimed hellfire mortar at was being incorrectly
remembered in a way that would force subsequent spells (including direct
projectiles) to also aim there instead of at proper monster targets.

More properly fix eldritch tentacle death cleanup

While 970ca23 fixed an issue with the portal feature not disappearing, by
removing any cleanup from the monster death event itself, if the tentacle
died on another monster's turn (which is likely), the portal would remain
until the end of the player's *next* turn, preventing them from recasting
the spell until then.

Now, the portal will once again close immediately (but should no longer
sometimes leave around portal features either).

Fix an issue with eldritch portals not disappearing

When a tentacle died, we attempted to clear up its portal. However, this
had two issues:
* It only fired if the tentacle was on the portal itself
* It did not clear up the temporary terrain change

These didn't matter when the tentacle dies elsewhere, because the map
marker tick clears up the portal anyway. But the combination of the two
meant that if the tentacle died while on the portal, the portal never
disappeared.

We fix this by not removing the marker at all in this case, leaving the
terrain reversion handled in a single place.

Fix a softlock involving grunt_nemelex_the_gamble

Items marked as 'unobtainable' (currently used *only* in this single vault)
were deliberately not added to the stash tracker. New logic added in
2985acf made the incorrect assumption that if there was a visible item on
the ground, that it would always be added to the stash (resulting in a
crash from trying to add a null pointer to the stash).

However, not adding unobtainable items to the stash tracker had some other
older bugs - most notably that attempting to examine the item on the ground
would fail to see it at all (since the stash is used to construct the
results of xv). ie: If you xv'd an exciting item in this vault, you would
only see floor. This seems clearly incorrect to me.

To be honest, I am not 100% certain the overall value of this flag as used
in a single vault, but as a stopgap measure, I am adding unobtainable items
into the stash tracker and simply hiding them on stash *search*. This
perhaps should be revisited in future.

Don't assert on looking up the description of a flavour without one

monster_info store the attack properties of a monster at the time they
were last seen. This means they can sometimes have attack flavours that
have since been removed.

There is no reason to assert for this situation (and even if we forget to
add a desecription for a new attack flavour, asserting doesn't feel
appropriate here.)
Fix a clang compile warning (Ge0FF)
Unbrace

Hopefully fix cursor for ranged attacks 'sticking' to old dead targets

If you aimed a ranged attack at a monster and it survived, and you aimed it
again and killed it, the next time you tried to fire, the cursor would
snap to the location you last fired at (because it retained memory of the
location as well as the monster, and when the monster was no longer there,
used the location instead).

I think this bug existed prior to dfde840 but that commit fixed a
different bug that allowed this bug to manifest properly.

(...I admit that I am still not 100% sure that this doesn't result in some
other issue since this UI is fairly complicated, but fingers crossed.)
feat: show owned consumable counts in shops
Fix typos.

Fix a crash when xv-ing monsters with a reaching attack and throwing weapon

The throwing weapon would not be seen when first determining layout of the
attack table, and have no range entry for itself. So if the melee attacks
*did* need a range column, it would read past the end of the array for the
throwing weapon's range.

(Instead, just say they have LoS range.)

Fix Exposed increasing *all* damage, including attack damage (rypofalem)

I went to some trouble to route more parts of attacks through
attack::inflict_damage(), so that we could tell what damage came from
attacks or not, and then somehow never actually set the argument added in
962f017 to true there. Whoops...
Fix item stack hilights not displaying in console (Undo)

Grant a monster halo immediately upon stealing a weapon while having none

Just in case you disarm Maurice *before* he swipes your Eos.

Slightly change internal ordering of monster unequipping

As a more thorough fix to follow e5056c4 this makes monster::unequip
directly unlink the item (so that an agrid invalidation won't see it) and
then calls do_unequip_effects() on its own.

The unlinked item must have something done with immediately afterward
(such as destroy it or place it on the grid), but this should currently be
done in all cases as it is, so I *believe* this should be safe.

Fix a test

The MAP_KNOWN_FLAG flag no longer exists, but a test was trying to use
it to set an area as known. Instead use the MAP_SEEN_FLAG flag as this
will work just as well to set an area as known.

Fix artefact and good item markers sometimes not showing

We were using multiple types to store map flags (such as int, uint32_t,
and uint64_t). This resulting in us accidentally clearing the
MAP_MORE_ITEMS_GOOD and MAP_MORE_ITEMS_ARTEFACT flags in
map_cell::set_door_connect as they can't be stored in the uint32_t that
it was using.

Fix out of view toxic bog not disappearing until game reload

When the player moves out of sight of their toxic bog it ends.
However, we weren't redrawing the squares where it had ended so they
wouldn't see this unless they reloaded the game.

Stop-gap measure to stop crashes when killing monsters above lava

A monster dropping equipped items into lava was producing a crash as of
febc422. This should stop said crashes, but will result in incorrect
behavior regarding certain items (such as halo/umbra-granting equipment)
that fall into lava this way.

I am putting a stop-gap measure in place to avoid the most urgent issue
since there are some complexities with fixing this more properly.

Fix unmarshalling 64 bit map flags

We were storing the map flags in an `unsigned int` when unmarshalling
them which caused the MAP_MORE_ITEMS_GOOD and MAP_MORE_ITEMS_ARTEFACT
flags to be lost as they require more than 32 bits to store.

Use latest Windows SDK

Using the old Windows 8.1 SDK was causing MSVC build errors.

Fix being able to use Bestial Takedown while netted (Planckenstein)

Even more comically, it didn't actually interfere with your attacks (since
that is checked outside of melee_attack itself), so you'd just leap around
with this decorative net on top of you.

Fix fortress crab not doubling artprop regen (Mandarbmax)

Due to the unusual way ARTP_REGENERATION is queried (as a consequence of
regen items needing to attune to the player individually, such that we
cannot simply check their combined sum), fortress crab's armour property
doubling wasn't affecting it at all.

(There's probaby a nicer way to structure this that allows
_player_bonus_regen() to use the artprop cache - possibly by specifically
only caching ARTP_REGENERATION off attuned items and calling
you.equipment.update() whenever an item becomes attuned. But I'm leaving
that for another time.)

Mention Exegesis's ability to be recast for cheaper (Midn8)

Mildly awkward given that the ability's name is based on the spell it's
recasting, but hopefully this is at least marginally clearer.
Fix missing -Jolt status description (Dilly)
Mention fortress crab's ability to wield two-handers in one hand (ssm_)
Add another name.

Fix wording.

Consistently use possessives before gerunds.

Fix pronoun.

Gods have no pronouns, not even "they."
Fix wording.

Fix another compiler warning

Since spret::seen_hups was added. (But it's not possible to get that return
value via this code path anyway, I'm fairly sure.)
Fix a couple compiler warnings with the debug version (rypofalem)
Fix tag upgrade build

Edit a pronoun in Goji's description to reduce confusion (apparently)

I was using 'they' in a gender-neutral sense in the last sentence (and
because I felt it had better cadence), rather than as a statement about
Goji's own gender. However, a surprising number of people interpreted it as
inconsistent with the use of he/him earlier in the description and now that
I've seen someone argue that this means Goji must be the name of the
*moth*, I am conceding that maybe I am the weird one in thinking it reads
completely naturally as it is.

Give sphinxes a chance to spawn with a barding

And increase drop rates slightly across the board

Remove an awkward method used to force autopickup

When an item became identified, if its unidentified state had been flagged
for autopickup, a prop was used to force autopickup to remain on after it
was identified.

This had some awkwardnesses, since this prop would *force* autopickup to
remain on for that item, no matter else might later tell it to turn off,
including .rc scripts (such as the one used by default to avoid autopickup
of redundant jewellery), becoming useless at a later time, and even
toggling it off with the autopickup menu.

While in *most* cases, said item would be picked up immediately, sometimes
this was not the case (most commonly with Ash, where you can ID items from
a distance). So if, for instance, you ID'd an rPois ring from a distance,
but were unable to pick it up (perhaps it was in a vault), then found
another rPois ring, the original ring would remain on autopickup forever,
despite the game saying that picking it up was pointless. Similar problems
could happen with an item later becoming literally useless (perhaps due to
gaining a slot-blocking mutation).

While I cannot be certain, I wonder if this may also be the root cause of
a rare-but-recurring bug people have reported with redundant rings being
picked up (which I could never reproduce).

In any case, identification works fairly different now than when this hack
was first added, and I am hoping it's no longer doing anything
load-bearing. (And if it is, then the root cause of that should be
addressed in a better way.)

Pick up missing aux armour by default

This snippet was available in advanced_optioneering.txt for quite a while,
but it's something players have asked about repeatedly and it feels like a
reasonable thing to simply make default now (especially since inventory
space isn't at a premium these days).

Allow Maurice to actually use melee weapons he steals

Maurice can equip and use ranged weapons they steal from the player, but if
they steal a melee weapon, they will just stick it in their secondary
weapon slot and never actually use it (preventing them from ever stealing a
ranged weapon at a later time, in fact.)

He can already pick up and wield melee weapons from the ground, and I'm
pretty sure the original intention of their code was for them to wield
melee weapons they steal (but the function names were misleading at the
time it was first written; see c625362)

Make Apportation pull entire item stacks at once

Apportation previously pulled only the top item of a stack. But it was
possible to somewhat manipulate this item by saving/reloading, and since
cb843fb03 the visible item at the top of the pile no longer has any direct
relation to what item is at the top of the stack internally.

To avoid a confusing relationship between what you see and what you pull,
instead pull *all* items on a given tile towards the player.

(It's theoretically possible to pull some random subset of these items, but
other devs seem to be of the opinion that a buff to the spell of this
nature is inconsequential - in the most common case of grabbing runs or the
orb, there's only one item on the tile anyway. If that turns out not to be
the case, it's easy to adjust it further.)

Don't go to extra trouble to move gold to the top of piles with Gozag

Gold will usually now display on top of mundane items anyway (since it's
flagged for autopickup), which seems sufficient to me.

(And if anyone really feels that it should always be on top of everything,
that is easy to do now by simply modifying _item_sort_score())

Improve display of item stacks on the ground (Ge0FF)

When multiple items are in a stack on the ground, only the top item in the
stack is displayed and an icon is added to indicate that more items are
beneath that one.

However, our implementation of this had several awkwardnesses. For one
thing, which item is on 'top' of a stack is largely coincidental (it's just
whichever fell last, which often depends on the order of items in a
monster's inventory). This means that important items are often hidden by
junk (and we don't even display the autopickup hilight on stacks that
contain autopickupable items, unless that item is on the top).

Moreover, the order of items in a stack isn't actually marshalled, so it
often *changes* whenever the player saves/reloads or peeks at another
floor. This can even be used tactically to change which item Apportation
will grab (since it always starts from the top of the stack).

This commit makes numerous changes aimed at making it easier to notice
interesting or important items in a stack (while Apportation itself will
be adjusted in a subsequent commit).

Items in stacks are now sorted based on some rough idea of their importance
to the player. This is approximately:
 autopickup-enabled -> artefacts -> branded and other special items ->
 everything else.

This increases the chance that player-relevant items will the ones which
are visible.

On top of this, the 'items are underneath here' marker now comes in 3
styles, indicating the presence of artefacts, special items, or only
mundane ones beneath the top item.

This means that the player can now often tell at a glance whether any
nearby piles could contain an artefact (rather than having to examine them
individually) and autopickup-able stacks should always show an autopickup
hilight.

This is implemented via the stash tracker itself (which now sorts items by
some criteria and can be asked to populate a map cell with the appropriate
flags). This is *arguably* not the proper place for it, but since it was
already doing a bunch of similar work about examining the properties of
items in a tile, I didn't want to duplicate its effort again outside it
(we already discard and regenerate stashes in sight multiple times every
turn as it is.)

This does mean, however, that update_item_at() should only be called after
stashes in sight have been regenerated. (Which I *think* should generally
be the case now.)
Fix a comment

Allow fravashi to pick up equipment

This is more consistent with other humanoid holies.

(They will still stick to polearm weapons, though, which are mechanically
useful as a summoner.)

Make efreets medium-sized

I was surprised to learn they were not (perhaps especially because of how
djinn-like they are in flavour) and this feels more appropriate to me.

(If someone feels otherwise, I'm not married to this.)

Give monsters a proper aux armour slot

Multiple monsters deliberately use aux armour as part of their normal gear,
but there's never been a proper slot for it, and convincing monsters to
wear it has involved a series of increasingly tortured hacks over the
years. For instance, Gastronok wears their hat in their body armour slot
(which was fine since they can't use other items). Then Robin wanted a
helmet, but they actually use body armour, so they wear it in their shield
slot. But then Wiglaf wanted a hat and they already had both body armour
*and* a shield, so they wear it in their ring slot.

There's been enough cases of these specific 'wear specific aux armour X in
specific other slot Y' that it feels useful to just give monsters an actual
aux armour slot. (Conveniently, we have been keeping around a dummied out
and never used slot in their equipment array for the last decade+ anyway.)

This commit implements said aux slot, and moves most monster aux equipment
into it. Alas, this cannot *completely* remove the aforementioned hacks
as a small number of monsters use multiple pieces of aux armour at once
(eg: Nikola uses gloves and a cloak), but is hopefully at least an
improvement in clarity.

Monsters can now also pick up aux armour in general (and there is a simple
function which should veto most nonsensicle combinations, like centaurs
wearing boots). This errs on the side of simplicity over thoroughless -
it's more important to avoid obviously incorrect combinations rather than
ensure all plausible combinations are possible.

(I also slightly improved the formatting of descriptions of monsters
wearing multiple pieces of gear at once.)

Fix monsters not getting an AC bonus from shields of protection

As far as I can tell, this has possibly never worked. Certainly not for
a very, very long time.

Allow goblin riders to pick up equipment

But since their tile has a spear baked into it, restrict them to other
polearms they can wield.

Separate the body/torso size of some monsters

In much the same way that player naga are able to wear medium-sized items
on their upper body, despite otherwise being large.

This also applies to rider monsters (ie: goblin riders should wield items
as if they are small, despite the wyvern they're on being larger).

(This does mean that it is now possible for centaurs to put on more types
of body armour they run across, which *might* be a concern in the
earlygame, though I am not sure it will happen commonly enough to matter.)

Tweak/improve monster equipment pickup logic

The logic used to control whether a monster considered a piece of equipment
on the ground to be better than what they were currently using was very old
and contained a bunch of... dubious valuations. For instance, it considered
most weapon brands to be exactly equivalent to a +2 enchantment (meaning a
+0 rapier was considered stronger than a +0 distortion dagger). Many
unrands did 'okay' on accont of generally having high plusses, but (for
instance) a +2 scimitar was considered stronger than Gyre and Gimble.

This attempts to make that a little more reasonable (generally making
monsters more strongly prefer branded weapons and especially strongly
prefer unrands - which are more memorable to the player, even if in some
cases not automatically stronger.). It doesn't bother to look at artprops
directly (and I think this is largely not worth the effort), but I think
the shape of this should still be an improvement.

As for armour, it now values resists much more highly (which it did check
already, but considered each pip equivalent to only 1 AC) and no longer
cares about Rampaging (which it valued at 5 AC, despite not even working on
monsters....)

Also, armour pickup had a check that universally prevented all monsters
with any wizardly spells from using any armour heavier than leather. This
included such spindly wizards as: vault wardens and vampire knights (and
so forth). Obviously, spell failure doesn't exist for monsters, but there's
still a certain flavor logic to monsters like annihilators not grabbing
the first plate armour they put their eyes on. So instead, this check now
prevents them from picking up armour that is more encumbering than whatever
they were already wearing (unless they have the fighter flag, in which case
they can wear anything).

Monsters will now try a little harder to hold onto their shields (only
switching to a two-hander if it is a major damage increase, as opposed to
'any damage increase').

Finally, a couple tweaks other tweaks:
 -Imperial Myrmidons no longer try to avoid picking up a weapon that isn't
  a long blade (this code was in the wrong place and never actually worked,
  but it doesn't seem compelling to me to fix it instead of remove it)
 -Maggie/Margery will only wear dragon scales (now that spellcasters can
  actually pick up heavier armour, they might otherwise have lost their
  signature look).

Most of this code isn't very load-bearing these days, since the player
can't actually *see* the monsters making terrible decisions, but it seems
better to be vaguely more reasonable.

Rename a couple deprecated weapon brands to reduce confusion

SPWPN_FLAME is overly similar to SPWPN_FLAMING, considering it's a removed
brand. Try to make it a little less likely to use the wrong one by mistake.

Fix a minor issue with cursor memory when targeting

If the player manually targeted a space that affected nothing with a spell
or other ranged attack, the UI was supposed to remember that spot for the
next time the player aims something (until they move). At some point, this
behavior seemed to get lost and a bunch of code was setting
you.prev_grd_targ without ever reading it.

(This may be minorly helpful in situations where the player is aiming at
invisible creatures.)

Refactor and tidy a bunch of agrid handling code

This commit does several things to slightly tidy and reorganize areas.cc
and related code:

-Removes some dummied enum members whose save compat code was completely
 unnecessary, since they were never marshalled anywhere.
-Reduces boilerplate for several common patterns.
-Removes an enum type whose presence was effectively duplicating another
 one.
-Inverts the default argument to invalidate_agrid() (since the other mode
 is needed in extremely few places by comparison).
-Unifies handling of items that affect the agrid into a new method,
 item_affects_agrid(). So long as any new item/ego is added there, there's
 no need for bespoke calls to invalidate_agrid() anywhere
-Degeneralizes a couple player-specific checks
-Fixes a minor bug where polymorphed holies wouldn't immediately update
 their halo size to the one of their new form

Slightly refactor monster equip/unequip handling

do_unequip_effects() was handling messaging, post-removal cleanup, and also
potentially vetoing unequipping items (including because they were cursed,
even though monsters haven't been able to get cursed items in years).

This commit removes various checks for cursed monster items and splits
do_unequip_effects() into two different functions: one for messaging and
another for internal cleanup, which can safely be called *after* the item
is actually removed. (This will be important for a subsequent commit.)

Also fix a minor bug where a launcher-wielding enemy who picks up a melee
weapon will falsely claim to immediately wield it, despite not doing so.

Don't bother specially tracking the Orb of Zot's location

Including updating it when the player drops it, which hasn't been possible
since ca22271 (14 years ago).

None of this code has served a purpose since ZotDef was removed. The aura
from it is only rendered when the player is holding it, so just use the
player's position as its center.

Remove some nonsensical code and comment

The comment refers to a draft version of paragon rather different than the
one that ever reached master (which cannot equip launcher at all).

But even then, the code doesn't at all do what the comment implies, nor
does it make any sense. Rather than preventing paragons from unequipping
their weapons, it allows any dancing weapons which are somehow *also*
paragons to unequip themselves from themselves.

What in the world was I thinking when I wrote this?

Extend map_cell.flags to 64-bits

Since we've basically run out of space and some upcoming content wants more
of them.

Don't leak the presence of halos or umbras via xv

xv-ing a tile inside a halo or umbra brought up a description of those
things, but this even worked for tiles out of LoS and was based on real
information, not remembered info.

This meant that if one was extremely methodical, you could, say, pinpoint
the location of Mennas on any previously seen tile. And if you used ?rev,
any tile in an entire unexplored level!

Display monster poison damage on xv (regret-index)

This can be calculated approximately as easily as elemental damage, so I'm
not certain why it wasn't already listed there.

Rename AF_CRUSH to AF_CONSTRICT

I realize it's been named this since literally the day constriction was
first added to Crawl, but also... why? Is there really any good reason not
to be named what it actually does?

Allow specifying monster reach and cleaving per-attack, improve xv

A number of monster attack flavours included innate reaching or cleaving as
part of their effect. Many of these duplicated other attack flavours except
for the part where they had longer range (eg: AF_ACID vs. AF_REACH_TONGUE).

This system was a bit inflexible and meant needing to make new versions of
a given flavour whenever we wanted a monster with it to reach.

Also, some of these flavours (such as AF_REACH) were deliberately retained
by derived undead, preventing those monsters from inheriting any new attack
flavour that derived undead ought to have (eg: a snapping turtle simulacrum
couldn't do any cold damage since its AF_COLD was completely overriden by
AF_REACH).

Now, each monster attack can specify reaching range and whether it cleaves
as independent properties. This allows new combinations to be made flexibly
and also for more simulacra/spectrals to actually function fully.

I have deprecated all attack flavours that merely duplicated an existing
one, aside from their reach.

(This also fixes a small bug where starflowers' second attack actually had
range 3 instead of 2, since the reach range of a monster's longest-range
attack was being applied to any attack that reached at all.)

In addition, range is now listed as a separate columm in xv, for monsters
that have any attacks with range greater than 1 (or cleaving). This
considerably improves clarity in cases where the presence of reaching
previously forced xv to append '(if damage dealt)' multiple times
(sometimes even multiple times in a single line!). The extra range from
polearms is also indicated, which could potentially make it clearer when
some of a monster's attacks are benefitting from their range and others
are not.

Refactor calculation of cleaving targets

get_cleave_targets() was used in multiple locations as a way to calculate
all targets in the player's attack range, even for non-cleaving attacks.
But since get_cleave_targets() itself also checked whether an attack
*should* cleave, this meant additional parameters to specifically bypass
this check (and some places that had to handle aqua form reaching
manually).

Instead, get_player_attack_targets() now provides this functionality (ie:
'list all targets in the range of any player weapon') without needing
parameters.

get_cleave_targets() now relies on the caller to have previously checked
whether an attack 'should' cleave (and at what range), which is done in
melee_attack::cleave_setup() in the common case.

This commit also fixes a handful of bugs:

-Since Coglins were added, the functionality of showing targets in cleave
 range when the player pressed v with a cleaving weapon was lost (even for
 players only wielding an axe). This is restored and improved to proper
 handle different combinations of weapons
-Coglins wielding a cleaving and non-cleaving weapon were often not
 prompted about attacks which might cause penance due to cleaving (never,
 if the cleaving weapon was in their off-hand, and only 50% of the time if
 it was in their main hand). The attack warning should now properly check
 both weapons all of the time.
-Coglins performing a reaching attack while a polearm and an axe would do
 nothing at all with their axe (even if other enemies were adjacent to
 them). Now it should also perform an attack with the axe in this case
 (equivalent to an 'empty' cleave against empty space).

Improve All-Purpose Tempering's valid target criteria

(ie: the monster version of Tempering)

Can no longer affect Vv or piles of debris, but *can* affect splinterfrost
barricades.

Fix emergency flight sometimes interacting oddly with temp forms

If the player's default form could survive in deep water, but their current
form can not, the game would think the water was dangerous for them in
some places and not in others.

As an example, if temporary flight expired over deep water, the player
would get a message about them falling into the water and emergency flight
activating every single turn, but it would never actually drain them.

Now, when checking for permanent swimming, we check *both* the player's
default form and current form.

(It's possible this may have some side-effects, but hopefully that is
fixing other niche bugs and not introducing new ones; it's not obvious to
me that there's any case where we want to know if a player can *usually*
swim if they also can't swim *currently*)

Don't give miasma-immunity or prevent berserking while under DDoor

Miasma immunity was originally given to DDoor in 6c7b304 to prevent getting
rotted by it. Miasma hasn't caused rot in years, but even then it had
other side-effects. DDoor doesn't generally prevent the player from
accumulating poison or gaining status effects, and it's not clear why it
should in this very narrow case.

The logic for not allowing the player to berserk while under DDoor may
possibly have been that you're not 'alive' enough, however almost all
places in code that aren't dealing damage otherwise treat a DDoor player as
properly living. There are a *lot* of effects that would interact differently
if we considered the player partially non-living or undead during this
status, and it doesn't feel like the spell would benefits from that
additional complexity. So instead, I am removing the couple tiny cases
where it seemingly tries. (To be clear, going berserk still won't actually
give you any additional HP - that is capped somewhere else.)

Abort Heal Other for too high target HP *before* the failure check

If the player's invo skill was too low to ever pacify a monster, the UI
would abort without taking time or consuming resources. But it previously
rolled the chance to fail to use the ability *before* checking whether
using it successfully was impossible.

Hide tile-only keys in the level map help outside tile mode.

The [ and ] keys had been included in the help for the level map
command with "(tiles only)" in their description. Drop this, and only
show the text in tile modes.

Make the lua function dgn.vault_at return a pointer

The lua function dgn.vault_at was returning a copy of the
vault_placemnt at a location. Unfortunately, it is slow to copy a
vault_placement and because the object returned to lua is a wrapper
around a c++ object lua doesn't know how big it is and won't trigger
garbage collection until you have about 8000 of them (about 17 MB).

The only place using dgn.vault_at is the disco Pan colour function which
can work just fine with a pointer rather than a copy and runs
considerably faster.

This is also consistent with the c++ equivalent that returns a pointer.

Fixes #3902

Fix seed stability for unrand weapon generation

Following f74bb9b, the Lochaber axe would be a candidate for different
items depending on the player's skill, and gyre and gimble wouldn't be a
candidate item for any short blade. We fix these checks not to use the
full unrand.

Fix crash in unrand checks for apostles

Since 5af3d4bd, we weren't sufficiently defining the unrand we checked
in could_wield, and so were crashing when trying to give unrands to
apostles. As well as fixing this crash, we make these unrands
sufficiently defined to check for monster-illegal unrands, and no longer
sometimes give these to monsters.

Remove an obsolete test

This tests Depths:3 generates the Abyss entry, which it doesn't any
more. There isn't a like-for-like replacement because the generation is
now a range of levels.

Add a connectivity check for totally isolated dungeon areas.

We check for areas which:
- Cannot reach a non-hatch staircase by flying
- Have at least one floor tile (excludes boxes of lava etc)

This treats vaults as opaque, like our main connectivity check.

The reason we use flying travel as the bar here is that various
transparent vaults have hatches which are isolated by deep water, and
these should not be vetoed.

In testing:
 * This has a rather low veto rate - around 0.03% of all levels.
 * Manually examining 10 vetoes, I see 8 good ones of varying severity -
   including two Ziggurat entrances the player would never have seen -
   and two acceptable false positives where the level is connected but
   only through an opaque vault.
 * There were no vaults that systematically got vetoed in a large
   mapstat (though it is hard to rule out there being some very rare
   vault that is now unplaceable)

Some representative vetoes can be seen on the PR #5346.

Fixes #2444

Move stone stair fixups before connectivity checks

We check our dungeon levels are accessible (including by using stone
stairs), but we were doing this before we culled extra stairs. This
reverses the order of those things.
